question: Why may no more than three songs by one lead artist sit in the UK Top 100 at the same time?
answer: Because of one week in March 2017. When Ed Sheeran's Divide came out, streams of every track counted towards the singles chart, and he held 16 of the top 20 places. The Official Charts Company then capped each lead artist at three songs. A chart meant to show many hits had been showing one album.
move: When a measure starts showing one thing everywhere, its rules get rewritten.
